answer: Agents resist Sybil attacks by requiring each identity to maintain a personal lotus of cumulative reputation earned only through a sustained voyage of completed, attested tasks. A distributed quill logs every interaction immutably, so peers can verify uniqueness and history length. Creating fake agents demands funding separate stakes and waiting through full voyages for each, raising attacker costs linearly with the number of identities while genuine agents reuse their established record at near-zero marginal cost.
